report:
Audit scope: src/provider/anthropic.rs 1-757.

## Findings

### F1. OpenAI string `stop` copied verbatim into stop_sequences → upstream 400 (Medium)
- location: src/provider/anthropic.rs:241-247
- category: type/API contract violation
- evidence:
if let Some(stop) = body.get("stop_sequences").or_else(|| body.get("stop")).filter(|v| !v.is_null()) {
    out["stop_sequences"] = stop.clone();
}
- scenario: OpenAI wire allows string stop ("stop": "END") — valid /v1 proxy client input. String lands in stop_sequences; Anthropic requires an array → 400 on every request. Array case unaffected, so only some clients hit it.
- fix: wrap string as [stop]; drop empty/null.

### F2. Mid-stream overloaded_error mapped to generic error — RateLimited retry path lost (Medium)
- location: src/provider/anthropic.rs:652-673 (error event branch)
- category: error handling/recovery
- evidence:
Some("error") => {
    done = true;
    let msg = v["error"]["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("upstream stream error");
    return Some((Err(anyhow::anyhow!("anthropic stream error: {msg}")), ...));
}
(HTTP layer :384-387, :417-421 does map 429/529 to RateLimited.)
- scenario: Anthropic delivers post-start overloads as an SSE error event with type "overloaded_error". This branch ignores v["error"]["type"] and always yields a plain anyhow error → runtime's RateLimited backoff/retry classification never applies; long tool-loop turns hard-fail visibly on overload.
- fix: promote to Err(RateLimited(..).into()) when type is overloaded_error/rate_limit_error; check policy for already-emitted partial output before retry.

### F3. Non-invertible mangle — legit `__` names corrupted and name collisions (Low)
- location: src/provider/anthropic.rs:445-447 (mangle), 453-458 (unmangle)
- category: correctness/boundary
- evidence:
fn mangle(name: &str) -> String { name.replace('.', "__") }
fn unmangle(name, names) -> names.get(name).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| name.replacen("__", ".", 1))
- scenario: (a) upstream-invented tool_use with a name containing __ but no dot (a__b) misses the names map → replacen mangles it to a.b, a nonexistent tool call at runtime. (b) tools a.b and a__b defined together both mangle to a__b; the map keeps the later one, so half of responses unmangle to the wrong tool.
- fix: collision-safe encoding (e.g. '.' -> '-dot-') or check fallback against the map's mangled key set.

## Clean (dedup material for next audit)
- SSE buffering/UTF-8: \n boundary slicing + from_utf8_lossy safe across chunk/UTF-8 splits (484-503)
- EOF without trailing newline feeds forced \n; EOF-without-message_stop surfaced as error, not clean Done (726-753)
- Usage double-count prevention: message_start baseline + saturating_sub in message_delta (516-524, 636-651)
- Dense tool index (tool_count), not sparse block index (495-515)
- tool_use block: id/name at content_block_start; partial_json accumulation owned by consumer runtime
- Thinking signature/block replay, redacted_thinking verbatim, cur_is_thinking reset on content_block_start (525-566)
- Request folding: user/tool runs into single user msg with tool_result first, empty content dropped (110-135)
- Thinking budget raises max_tokens when budget >= max_tokens (285-303); thinking dropped when tool history lacks thinking blocks (306-315)
- cache_control on last system block and last message's last block (318-338)
- 401 OAuth force-refresh retry once (337-345, 395-403); 429/529 → RateLimited (384-387, 417-421)
- Non-stream chat: stop_reason mapping tool_use→tool_calls, max_tokens→length (423-430)

## Notes / not audited
- retry_after/RateLimited/content_text implementations live in src/provider/mod.rs (other scout's scope); F2's downstream classification should be cross-checked against runtime.rs's RateLimited consumption.
- tool_choice "none" → {"type":"none"} (255-257): could not verify Anthropic API support offline; not submitted as a finding.
- tests/providers.rs left to TestsProviders scouts.
summary: Full audit of src/provider/anthropic.rs (1-757). SSE parsing itself (byte buffering, UTF-8 chunk boundaries, missing trailing newline, usage double-count prevention, truncated-stream EOF) is solid. 3 defect candidates: (1) OpenAI string stop copied verbatim into stop_sequences causing upstream 400 (Medium), (2) mid-stream overloaded_error mapped to a generic error, losing the RateLimited retry path (Medium), (3) non-invertible mangle corrupts legit tool names containing __ and collides a.b/a__b (Low).
